issuing_body: Parliament of Malaysia (Royal Assent: Yang di-Pertuan Agong)
title_english: Electricity Supply Act 1990
notes: Royal Assent 22 Aug 1990; Gazette 30 Aug 1990 (ST reprint as at 1 Jul 2016, read). s.9 licences for every installation (public and private, i.e. including own-use/captive); s.26 tariffs; s.50A codes; s.50C guidelines; s.54 exemptions. Suspended in Sarawak from 1 Sep 1990 (P.U.(A) 272/1990). Not applied by ST in Sabah since 3 Jan 2024 (ECoS); the federal instrument for that was not located. Amended by A1116 (2001; not a row), A1501, A1739 and A1775. Malay text is authoritative.

title_english: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2015
notes: Royal Assent 30 Oct 2015; Gazette 5 Nov 2015; in force 1 Jan 2016 (ST reprint list of amendments). Creates the Single Buyer (s.22B) and System Operator (s.22A) with ring-fencing, codes (s.50A), binding guidelines and directions (s.50C) with an offence for non-compliance (s.50E), the Electricity Industry Fund. The official LOM PDF path returned HTTP 500; the source is the ESCAP summary.

title_english: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2024
notes: Royal Assent 2 Jul 2024; Gazette 26 Nov 2024; in force 1 Jan 2025 by P.U.(B) 520/2024 (per search snippet; the e-aset host was unreachable). Deletes 'efficient use of electricity' and Part VA from Act 447; those move to the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act 2024 (Act 861). Peripheral to power-sector rules.

title_english: Electricity Supply (Amendment) Act 2025
notes: Text read: Royal Assent 31 Oct 2025; Gazette 18 Nov 2025; passed Dewan Rakyat 30 Jul 2025 and Dewan Negara 9 Sep 2025 (press). Adds licensing of electricity import and export (s.22D), defines 'green attributes', and creates a 'Market Operator' (s.22C). STATUS UNCONFIRMED: commencement is by ministerial notification (possibly staged) and no P.U.(B) notice was found. 'in force' is a placeholder because the schema has no 'pending' status. Applies to the Peninsula and Labuan only.

title_english: Energy Commission (Amendment) Act 2025
notes: Date is the Gazette date (per the ST performance booklet seen in search results; not opened); Royal Assent not confirmed. Amends the Energy Commission Act 2001 (Act 610; not a row) to give ST regulatory functions over electricity import and export. Commencement not confirmed (see A1775).

title_english: Renewable Energy Act 2011
notes: Sets the feed-in tariff system (feed-in approvals by SEDA, distribution licensees obliged to buy, RE fund levy). Covers the Peninsula and Labuan; Sabah moved to its own enactment in 2024. Exact Royal Assent, Gazette and commencement dates not checked (FiT began in 2011). Companion: SEDA Act 2011 (Act 726). Key subsidiary rules: RE (Feed-in Approval and FiT Rate) Rules 2011, P.U.(A) 385/2011, amended e.g. by P.U.(A) 366/2020.

title_english: Renewable Energy (Amendment) Act 2023
notes: Royal Assent 22 Jul 2023; Gazette 28 Jul 2023 (text read). Among other changes, it adds s.1(3) letting the Minister suspend the Act in parts of Malaysia, which appears to prepare for Sabah's RE Enactment 2024 (our inference). Other amendments not reviewed. Commencement notice not found; 'in force' is a placeholder.

issuing_body: Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (s.63 Act 725)
title_english: Renewable Energy (Amendment of Schedule) Order 2025
notes: Made 1 Aug 2025; deemed in operation from 28 Jan 2019. Extends the FiT effective period for biogas items (b)(i)-(iii) from 16 to 21 years. A ministerial order in the Federal Gazette, mapped to 'government regulation'. Earlier schedule orders: P.U.(A) 131/2022 (biogas cap 5 MW to 30 MW), P.U.(A) 347/2020, P.U.(A) 222/2017.

title_english: Guidelines for New Enhanced Dispatch Arrangement
notes: ST guideline under s.50C Act 447 (binding; mapped to 'circular'). Version record: v2.0 17 Apr 2017; Pin.2019 28 May 2019 (adds solar power producers); Pin. No.2/2019 5 Dec 2019; Pin.2024 22 Nov 2024 (CRESS, CGPP and LSS participation); Pin.2025 26 Dec 2025 (CREAM). Merchant dispatch layer run by the Single Buyer at the system marginal price; the settlement platform for CGPP, CRESS and CREAM. Peninsula only.

title_english: Guidelines for Single Buyer Market (Peninsular Malaysia) 2018
notes: s.50C guideline. Registered 18 Apr 2018; revised 1 Nov 2024 (signed 18 Nov 2024; ST listing 22 Nov 2024). Rules for the Single Buyer's planning, scheduling, procurement and settlement, plus ring-fencing practices (Annex 2). A 32 MB PDF; the first download was truncated.

issuing_body: Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga), approved by the Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation
title_english: Grid Code for Peninsular Malaysia - Main Code
notes: Code under s.50A Act 447 (mapped to 'circular'; codes may deserve their own type). Dated 28 Mar 2025; in force 1 Jan 2026. Comes with an Additional Code (glossary and sub-codes). Appears to replace the Grid Code for Peninsular Malaysia KOD/ST/No.2/2010, which the CRESS guidelines still cite, but no revocation clause was found in the first 30 pages.

title_english: Guidelines for Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS)
notes: s.50C guideline. First version effective 20 Sep 2024 (Skrine); second version 1 Mar 2025; third version 29 Dec 2025 (signed 26 Dec 2025; listed 6 Jan 2026). Third-party access: a renewable energy developer supplies a green consumer over the network in the Peninsula and pays a system access charge (SAC) through the Single Buyer. 51% local ownership is a licence condition. SAC 25/45 sen/kWh firm/non-firm at launch; PETRA cut it to 20/40 sen for RP4 on 29 Aug 2025 (press release PETRA.100-9/1/4 JLD.1 (39)). See also MY-DEC-2026-CAP.

issuing_body: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA)
title_english: CRESS Acceleration Package (fixed system access charge for early projects)
notes: PETRA press release of 18 Sep 2026 (Malay) plus the ST SAC and criteria sheets. SAC fixed at 14.0 sen/kWh (developer, firm) and 4.02 sen/kWh (green consumer) for 10 years from COD; minimum 10-year contract; COD by 31 Dec 2028, otherwise the prevailing SAC applies, with no extensions. 11 developers and 8 consumers (3,148 MW) were registered by then. The SAC method will change from RP5 (2028). The ST page says the guideline text is 'to be updated', so this is a decision not yet codified; link it to the CRESS revision when one appears.

title_english: Guidelines for Community Renewable Energy Aggregation Mechanism (CREAM)
notes: s.50C guideline; first version, registration date not shown in the PDF. Applications from 1 Jun 2025. A local energy generator and aggregator supplies local green consumers from community solar plants (100 kWp to 2 MWp per 11 kV feeder) over the distribution network in the Peninsula. Community access charge of 15 sen/kWh, cut to 9 sen/kWh for RP4 on 29 Aug 2025 (PETRA).

title_english: Guidelines for Solar Accelerated Transition Action Programme in Peninsular Malaysia
notes: s.50C guideline; registered 30 Dec 2025; in force 1 Jan 2026. Successor to NEM 3.0 (which closed to new applicants at the end of June 2025, per SEDA) but does not revoke the NEM guidelines. Exports are credited on energy only: the energy charge for domestic consumers and the average SMP for non-domestic. Caps: 5 kW single phase and 15 kW three phase for domestic; aggregate 1,000 kW otherwise. Open to consumers without existing solar or NEM, unless they terminate their NEM contract. SEDA is the implementing agency (eATAP system). ST lists two copies of the PDF (with and without _0).

title_english: Guidelines for Solar Photovoltaic Installation for Self-Consumption in Peninsular Malaysia
notes: s.50C guideline; in operation 1 Jan 2025. Revisions: Pin.2025 27 Mar 2025; Pin.1/2026 15 Jun 2026 (signed 21 Jul 2026, new definition of 'premise'). Revokes GP/ST/No.13/2017 (Pin.2023), Guidelines on the Connection of Solar PV Installation for Self-Consumption (not a row). ST notice of 31 Dec 2025: the standby charge of RM12/kWp applies above 1 MWac (previously 1 MWp), and BESS is required only above 1 MWac (previously above 72 kWp). A separate SELCO guideline covers Kulim Hi-Tech Park (2025).

title_english: Guidelines for Solar Photovoltaic Installation under the Programme of NEM Rakyat and NEM GoMEn in Peninsular Malaysia
notes: NEM 3.0 (announced by KeTSA on 29 Dec 2020; 2021-2025; up to 2,500 MW in all per SEDA). One-for-one offset for 10 years for homes (NEM Rakyat) and government premises (NEM GoMEn, up to 1,000 kW). Eight versions: 29 Jan 2021; 15 Jul 2023; 5 Feb 2024; 1 Apr 2024; 20 Sep 2024; 25 Nov 2024; 1 Mar 2025 (quota top-ups); 19 Aug 2026 (new tariff structure). Closed to new applicants on 30 Jun 2025 (SEDA) but still governs existing participants. Consider one row per quota revision.

title_english: Guidelines for Solar Photovoltaic Installation under Net Offset Virtual Aggregation (NOVA) Programme in Peninsular Malaysia
notes: NEM 3.0 track for non-domestic consumers (up to 1,000 kW; exports credited at the average SMP). Versions: 29 Jan 2021; 15 Jul 2023 (+500 MW); 5 Feb 2024 (+300 MW); 25 Nov 2024 (+300 MW); 1 Mar 2025 (+300 MW); 23 Jul 2026 (new tariff structure). Closed to new applicants on 30 Jun 2025 (SEDA).

title_english: Guidelines on Green Electricity Tariff
notes: s.50C guideline for TNB's Green Electricity Tariff (consumers pay an extra charge for renewable supply). Revisions: 25 Nov 2024 (subscription may be retrospective); 31 Jan 2025; 14 Jul 2025 (clause 6.5 and new 6.6 on mREC transfer). Revokes GP/ST/No.31/2022 (earlier GET guidelines; not a row). The original 2023 registration date is not shown.

title_english: Guidelines on Electricity Tariff Determination under Incentive-Based Regulation (IBR) for Peninsular Malaysia 2025
notes: Regulatory implementation guidelines issued under ss.26 and 50C. The date is the ST listing date (signature date not found in the PDF), so it is medium confidence. Sets the RP4 revenue-cap method, base average tariff, Automatic Fuel Adjustment (section 7), WACC and efficiency carry-over. Probably supersedes the IBR guidelines of 2018, 2021 and 2022 (all still listed); not confirmed.

issuing_body: Government of Malaysia (tariff approval under s.26 Act 447); announced by the Energy Commission
title_english: Electricity tariff schedule for Regulatory Period 4 (Peninsular Malaysia), 1 Jul 2025 - 31 Dec 2027
notes: ST media statement of 20 Jun 2025 (Malay). Average base tariff 45.40 sen/kWh (45.62 sen approved in Dec 2024; RP3 was 39.95 sen per press). New customer categories by voltage; separate energy, capacity, network and retail charges; energy-efficiency incentive (domestic 1,000 kWh/month or less); wider ToU off-peak. The monthly Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) replaces ICPT from Jul 2025; the 3 sen/kWh monthly cap without government approval is reported by the press only. No gazetted instrument found.

title_english: Guidelines on Licence Application under the Electricity Supply Act 1990 [Act 447] (2nd edition)
notes: 2nd edition (1st 2016; not a row); listed 27 Jan 2025. Public installation licences cover sales to utilities (IPP, LSS, FiT), own use with export (NEM, NOVA) and own use where a third party owns the asset (leasing or PPA). Private licences cover own use with a consumer-owned asset (diesel, solar, biogas). Online application for public licences and for private ones of 5 MW and above. Lists the s.54 exemptions P.U.(B) 156/1994, 342/2008, 307/2012 and 297/2024 (EV charging).

title_english: Guidelines on Large Scale Solar Photovoltaic Plant for Connection to Electricity Networks
notes: Revisions: 20 Dec 2018 (Pin.2019); 20 May 2020 (Pin.2020); 2 Apr 2024 (Pin.2024). Development framework, injection points, milestones to COD and licensing for LSS auction plants. The SEDA LSS page still links a dead 2019 copy at /contents/2019/LSS/.

issuing_body: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), through the Energy Commission
title_english: Notice of issue of Request for Proposal for the sixth Large Scale Solar competitive bidding round (LSS6)
notes: Notice dated 24 Jul 2026 (Malay). 2,650 MW solar and 1,250 MW/6,000 MWh BESS in the Peninsula: Package 1 open hybrid (2,200 MW + 1,100 MW BESS), Package 2 Bumiputera hybrid (300 MW + 150 MW BESS), Package 3 Bumiputera solar only (150 MW). RFP sales 27 Jul-7 Aug 2026 (hybrid) and 17-28 Aug 2026 (solar). COD target 31 Dec 2029 (press). Earlier rounds LSS4 (2020), LSS5 (RFP Apr 2024) and LSS PETRA 5+ (Jan 2025, 1,975 MWac awarded per press) are not rows yet.

issuing_body: Energy Commission, for the Ministry of Natural Resources, Environment and Climate Change (NRECC)
title_english: Corporate Green Power Programme (virtual PPA for solar)
notes: Launch date 7 Nov 2022 (600 MW) per law firms (Rahmat Lim). ST award notice: applications 9 May-31 Dec 2023 for an 800 MW quota, target commercial operation in 2025 through NEDA; 22 solar producers (563.42 MW) announced 7 Aug 2023. Corporate Green Power Agreement = virtual sale and purchase; the consumer stays a normal TNB customer. The information guide (April 2023) is not a registered GP/ST guideline. 'expired' means the application window has closed; the contracts continue.

issuing_body: Economic Planning Unit, Prime Minister's Department
title_english: National Energy Policy 2022-2040 (Dasar Tenaga Negara)
notes: Launched 19 Sep 2022 by PM Ismail Sabri (press). Low Carbon Nation Aspiration 2040; reviewed every three years by a National Energy Council. The NETR builds on it.

title_english: National Energy Transition Roadmap
notes: Phase 1 (10 flagship catalyst projects) launched 27 Jul 2023; Phase 2 (targets and pathway) 29 Aug 2023 (press; check the launch dates). Targets: 70% RE installed capacity by 2050 (up from 40% by 2040); 'No new coal power plant'; coal 'close to fully phased-out' of power generation by 2050. Coal exit by 2044 was announced by DPM Fadillah Yusof (Jun 2024; reaffirmed Jul 2026) but is not in an instrument. No separate public power development plan exists; the JPPPET 2024-2050 generation plan is unpublished.

issuing_body: Sabah State Legislative Assembly (assent: Yang di-Pertua Negeri)
title_english: Electricity Supply Enactment 2024 (Sabah)
notes: Assented and in operation 3 Jan 2024 (text read). Gives the Energy Commission of Sabah (ECoS) licensing (s.8), tariff, fund and safety powers in Sabah, replacing ST. Existing ST licences stay valid until amended or revoked (s.111). Paired with the Energy Commission of Sabah (Amendment) Enactment 2024 and a set of 2024 regulations. The title year (2024) differs from the enactment number year (2023). The id uses a state segment (SBH) outside the standard pattern.

issuing_body: Sabah State Legislative Assembly (assent: Yang di-Pertua Negeri)
title_english: Sabah Renewable Energy Enactment 2024
notes: Assented and in operation 3 Jan 2024. A Sabah feed-in tariff system under ECoS (replacing SEDA in Sabah): feed-in approvals, RE PPAs, priority purchase, degression, RE fund. Sabah FiT approval holders were transferred from SEDA to ECoS.

title_english: Electricity (Amendment) Ordinance 2023 (Sarawak), amending the Electricity Ordinance (Cap. 50)
notes: The date is the date the DUN passed the Bill; assent, gazette and commencement are unknown. Press and Sarawak Energy releases: makes Sarawak Energy the statutory Single Buyer; raises the licence-free solar threshold from 5 kW to 50 kW, with surplus sold under NEM; allows special agreements above 5 MW; solar producers may sell to other consumers if the Single Buyer does not need the power. The Cap. A210/2023 number comes from a LawNet reprint listing seen only in search results (LawNet and Sarawak Energy were unreachable: 000 and 403).
